import pandas as pd

# Load source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_10/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_10/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation: JOIN on "city"
# Source0 schema: ['city', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']
# Source1 schema: ['city', 'driver_count', 'type']
# Target schema: ['city': string, 'driver_count': integer]

# Join df0 and df1 on 'city'
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Select only the columns required by the target schema
result_df = joined_df[["city", "driver_count"]]

# Ensure correct data types
result_df["city"] = result_df["city"].astype(str)
result_df["driver_count"] = result_df["driver_count"].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_10/target_multisource.csv"
result_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_10/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_10/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' and aggregate driver_count by max (to ensure unique driver_count per city)
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({"driver_count": "max"})

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_10/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
